answers.justification: The article describes the trial as double-blind with placebo injections, which supports intended masking. However, nausea occurred in 27.4% and vomiting in 9.4% with lixisenatide versus 4.9% and 1.3% with placebo, and nausea/vomiting led to discontinuation only in the lixisenatide group. These marked, recognizable differences could have allowed some participants to infer their assignment, although the report does not state that participants actually recognized it.
unknowns: The report does not describe participants' actual guesses about assignment or formally assess whether masking was broken.

answers.justification: The study was double-blind and investigators did not have access to the allocation code, which supports intended masking. The substantially more frequent nausea and vomiting in the lixisenatide arm, including differential treatment discontinuations, could have led personnel interacting with participants to infer assignment. The report does not state that personnel actually became aware.
unknowns: Whether investigators, carers, or intervention personnel inferred or learned individual assignments is not reported.

answers.justification: The only described protocol-violation counts are two in the lixisenatide group; two further withdrawals were attributed to poor protocol compliance. The report does not say what actions occurred or whether the trial context caused them. Rescue therapy for one person per group was allowed under stated thresholds, so rescue itself is not evidence of a context-caused protocol deviation.
unknowns: Nature of the protocol violations and poor-compliance events.
Whether any such events were caused by trial participation and were inconsistent with protocol.

answers.justification: The efficacy analysis followed randomized assignment in the mITT population; registry flow reports all 223 randomized participants in each group in that population. The report defines mITT as randomized participants who received at least one dose and had baseline and at least one postbaseline efficacy assessment, with LOCF for missing efficacy values. The reported analysis did not reassign participants to groups or exclude randomized participants from the mITT population.
unknowns: LOCF may affect the estimated outcome, but the reported group sizes show no randomized participants omitted from the mITT analysis.
